mie.name: Make it in the Emirates — Awards Platform
mie.blurb: Government platform for the UAE Ministry of Industry & Advanced Technology. End-to-end ownership across frontend, backend, infra, and CI/CD.

caseStudy.problem: Deliver a government-grade, public-facing awards platform for the UAE Ministry of Industry & Advanced Technology — supporting 5,000+ concurrent users across applicants, jurors, and program operators with the security and uptime expectations of a government deployment.
caseStudy.architecture: Next.js frontend and NestJS backend over PostgreSQL with Prisma ORM. AWS infrastructure across VPC, EC2, RDS, S3, CloudFront, IAM, and Secrets Manager, with container-first pipelines (Docker → ECR → ECS via CodeBuild / CodePipeline). Vitest + React Testing Library + Playwright coverage, structured logging into CloudWatch, and SEO via server-side rendering and schema markup.
caseStudy.contributions: Owned end-to-end technical implementation across frontend, API surface, PostgreSQL schema, and AWS infrastructure. · Architected PostgreSQL schemas with Prisma ORM, targeted indexing, and query-tuning that cut API latency by 35% under production traffic. · Built domain-driven modules in Next.js and NestJS, reducing feature rollout time by 25%. · Established container-first deployment pipelines (Docker → ECR → ECS via CodeBuild / CodePipeline), cutting deploys from ~20 minutes to under 5. · Added CloudWatch monitoring and structured logging that reduced issue detection time by 40%. · Hardened the platform with JWT authentication, RBAC, structured validation, and a full Vitest / RTL / Playwright testing pyramid.

lawmate.name: LawMate — Legal Services Platform
lawmate.blurb: End-to-end, API-first legal-services platform built with Laravel and Filament — a request-and-bid marketplace connecting clients with lawyers, with an in-app Paymob wallet and real-time chat, voice, and SMS.

caseStudy.problem: Legal services in the region are fragmented and opaque — clients can't easily find the right lawyer or agree on a price, and firms have no structured backend to receive, bid on, and manage cases. LawMate needed an API-first backend that could run a request-and-bid marketplace with payments, real-time communication, and escalation handling behind a single bilingual platform.
caseStudy.architecture: API-first Laravel backend with Sanctum authentication, attribute-based routing, and self-validating DTOs, administered through a role-based Filament (Livewire) panel. MySQL for relational data and Redis for cache and queues. Real-time chat and voice/SMS via Laravel Reverb WebSockets and Twilio, Firebase Cloud Messaging for mobile push, and S3-backed media storage. Paymob powers the in-app wallet, payments, and withdrawals; Pest and PHPUnit cover the domain.
caseStudy.contributions: Built the API-first Laravel backend powering a request-and-bid workflow that connects clients with lawyers, plus escalation handling and an in-app wallet with Paymob payments and withdrawals. · Designed self-validating DTOs and attribute-based routing under Sanctum authentication. · Architected the platform for real-time chat and voice/SMS (Laravel Reverb WebSockets, Twilio), FCM mobile push, and S3-backed media storage, with bilingual EN/AR content. · Administered everything through a role-based Filament (Livewire) admin panel and backed the domain with Pest and PHPUnit test coverage.

sabeel.name: Sabeel — Mobile Backend
sabeel.blurb: Backend powering a high-traffic mobile product. Hardened the API surface, cut latency, and shipped reliable infra on AWS.

caseStudy.problem: A growing mobile app needed a backend that could handle thousands of concurrent users without latency spikes, plus a deploy pipeline the team could trust.
caseStudy.architecture: Laravel API on AWS ECS behind an ALB, MySQL on RDS, static assets through S3 + CloudFront. CI/CD through ECR with CodeBuild / CodePipeline, secrets in Secrets Manager, IAM-scoped access, and CloudWatch monitoring and alerts.
caseStudy.contributions: Architected normalized relational data models and optimised complex SQL queries, cutting API latency by 30% while supporting thousands of active mobile users. · Managed the full AWS production infrastructure (EC2, S3, IAM, RDS) — provisioning, deployment, monitoring, and maintenance. · Implemented secure authentication flows, input validation, and backend security best practices across the system. · Set up CloudWatch dashboards and alarms so on-call could spot regressions in minutes.

esl.name: Egyptian Schools League — Competition Engine
esl.blurb: Modular competition engine with real-time leaderboards. Replaced spreadsheet workflows with a configurable rules engine.

caseStudy.problem: Operators were running national school competitions out of spreadsheets — slow scoring, fragile state, and no real-time visibility for participants.
caseStudy.architecture: Next.js front-end, NestJS back-end with a modular rules engine, PostgreSQL via Prisma, and a Docker-based deploy. WebSockets for live leaderboard updates.
caseStudy.contributions: Engineered a modular competition engine covering team onboarding, scoring logic, and ranking algorithms. · Built the real-time leaderboard pipeline and the operator dashboards that consume it. · Reduced manual administrative workload by 80% and improved processing efficiency by 50% by replacing spreadsheet workflows with structured forms and validation.

wabot.name: WhatsApp AI Chatbot Automation
wabot.blurb: Serverless AI chatbot combining Amazon Lex and Twilio to automate customer-support workflows on WhatsApp.

caseStudy.problem: Support agents were drowning in repetitive WhatsApp inquiries — order status, hours, common FAQs — and customers waited hours for answers any bot could give in seconds.
caseStudy.architecture: Twilio webhook → AWS Lambda (Python) → Amazon Lex for intent + slot filling, with secrets in AWS Secrets Manager and CloudWatch for traceability. Pure event-driven: scales to zero between conversations.
caseStudy.contributions: Designed intent + slot taxonomy across the support team's real ticket history. · Wrote the Lambda orchestration that bridges Lex, Twilio, and the internal CRM. · Automated 60% of customer-support workflows and eliminated manual triage for common request types, escalating cleanly to a human when confidence dropped.

eltan.name: Eltanfeethi — Azure Delivery
eltan.blurb: Led Azure infrastructure, release pipelines, and production deployment for a client-facing application.

caseStudy.problem: A client-facing application needed Azure infrastructure stood up, an API gateway in place, and a release process the team could actually trust before going to production.
caseStudy.architecture: Azure compute + storage, Azure API Management fronting the service surface, release pipelines through Azure DevOps with environment gates.
caseStudy.contributions: Designed the Azure infrastructure layout — subscriptions, network, identity, and policy. · Configured API Management with the routing, throttling, and key-management the platform required. · Built the release pipelines and gates that took the platform from staging into a production rollout.

r1.b1: Full-stack engineer at Challenge Group — an AWS/Huawei Cloud partner delivering production platforms for government and enterprise clients across Egypt, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE.
r1.b2: Owned the Make it in the Emirates Awards platform (MoIAT) for the UAE Ministry of Industry & Advanced Technology from schema to deploy — domain-driven Next.js/NestJS modules over a PostgreSQL/Prisma schema serving 5,000+ concurrent users, with targeted indexing and query-tuning that cut API latency ~35% under production load.
r1.b3: Built the AWS infrastructure (VPC, EC2, RDS, S3, CloudFront, IAM, Secrets Manager) and a container-first Docker → ECR → ECS pipeline (CodeBuild / CodePipeline), reducing deploys from ~20 minutes to under 5.
r1.b4: Hardened platforms with JWT authentication, RBAC, structured validation, and API hardening; added CloudWatch monitoring and structured logging, a full test pyramid (Vitest, React Testing Library, Playwright), and SEO via SSR, structured metadata, and schema markup.
r1.b5: Built LawMate, an API-first Laravel legal-services platform (Filament admin, Sanctum, a Paymob wallet, and Reverb/Twilio real-time), and the Egyptian Schools League competition engine with real-time leaderboards.
r1.b6: Shipped a serverless WhatsApp AI support bot (AWS Lambda, Amazon Lex, Twilio), hardened the Sabeel mobile backend on AWS, and led the Eltanfeethi Azure delivery with Azure API Management and CI/CD.

r2.b1: Completed a government-sponsored, intensive software-engineering program (~1,200 hours) spanning full-stack development, system design, and cloud deployment.
r2.b2: Built full-stack applications across two backend ecosystems — Node.js/Express and Python (Django, Flask) — with React front-ends, secure REST APIs, structured authentication flows, and role-based access control.
r2.b3: Modeled both relational (SQL) and NoSQL databases, applying normalization and indexing to keep queries efficient as datasets grew.
r2.b4: Containerized services with Docker and deployed to AWS, applying system-design fundamentals and working in Agile sprints from design through delivery.

r3.b1: Built and shipped a production-ready e-commerce storefront in React — a responsive, cross-device UI wired to REST APIs for the product catalog and cart.
r3.b2: Architected a reusable component library with centralized state via React's Context API, removing prop-drilling and keeping catalog and cart state consistent as the product range and traffic grew.
r3.b3: Improved rendering performance and cut page-load times through render optimization and efficient asset loading, keeping large product listings smooth as the catalog scaled.

faq.label: FAQ
faq.a1: Paula Magdy is a full-stack software engineer based in Cairo, Egypt, with 3+ years of experience designing, building, and scaling production web platforms across frontend, backend, cloud, and DevOps.
faq.q2: What technologies does Paula Magdy work with?
faq.a2: He builds with Next.js, React, and TypeScript on the frontend; Node.js, NestJS, and Express, plus Laravel (PHP) and Django/Flask (Python) on the backend; PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, Redis, and Prisma ORM for data; and AWS, Azure, Huawei Cloud, Docker, and CI/CD for cloud and delivery.
faq.a3: Most recently he owned end-to-end delivery of the Make it in the Emirates Awards platform for the UAE Ministry of Industry & Advanced Technology — a government-grade system serving 5,000+ concurrent users — along with LawMate (an API-first legal-services platform), competition engines, mobile backends, and serverless AI automation at Challenge Group, an AWS/Huawei Cloud partner serving clients across Egypt, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE.
faq.q4: Where is Paula Magdy based, and is he open to remote work?
faq.a4: He is based in Cairo, Egypt, and is open to full-stack engineering roles and consulting engagements, including remote work.
faq.q5: What certifications does Paula Magdy hold?
faq.a5: He holds the AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Associate and AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner certifications, plus Huawei's HCCDP-Solution Architectures, HCCDA-Tech Essentials, and HCIA-AI — alongside a B.Sc. in Computer Science from October 6 University.
faq.q6: How can I get in touch with Paula Magdy?
faq.a6: You can reach him by email at paulamagdy665@gmail.com or through the contact form on this site — he typically replies within 24 hours.
